statement: The 2007 National Football Conference (NFC) Championship Game was an American football game played between the New York Giants and the Green Bay Packers on January 20, 2008, at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin, United States.
The Packers finished the season 13–3, winning the NFC North, while securing the second seed in the playoffs.
The Giants entered the playoffs as a Wild Card team, with a record of 10–6.
The Giants did not win the NFC East, which was won by the Dallas Cowboys, who secured the first seed in the playoffs via a head-to-head tiebreaker with the Packers.
The Giants beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and the Cowboys in the Wild Card and Divisional rounds, respectively.
The Packers beat the Seattle Seahawks in the Divisional round.
By virtue of their higher seeding, the Packers were given home field advantage for the Championship Game.
The game was a continuation of the two teams' rivalry, which included five NFL Championship Games from the 1930s to the 1960s.
The game was marked by cold weather, with the wind chill factor bringing the temperature down to −23 °F (−31 °C).
The game was the second coldest game in Lambeau Field history.
The teams went back and forth, with the Packers capitalizing on a 90-yard touchdown pass in the first half.
The Giants leaned on their running attack, outgaining the Packers in rushing yards 114 to 28.
The Giants missed two field goals, including a possible game-winner at the end of the fourth quarter that led to overtime.
The Packers had three turnovers, with Favre throwing an interception on the second play of overtime.
The Giants won the game on a walk-off field goal by Lawrence Tynes four plays after Favre's interception.
The Giants' victory sent them to Super Bowl XLII, where they would beat the New England Patriots.
The NFC Championship Game became part of the Giants–Packers rivalry.
The NFC Championship Game was notable for its competitiveness, cold weather, and impact on each team.
The game helped establish Eli Manning's career.
For Favre, the game became the last he would play for the Packers.
Favre was traded during the offseason to the New York Jets.
Aaron Rodgers was named starting quarterback for the Packers.
The New York Giants were coming off of a Wild playoff berth in 2006 with a record of 8–8.
The Giants began the season with two consecutive losses, including a 35–13 blowout loss to the Green Bay Packers in Week 2.
The Giants then won six straight games going into their bye week to bring their record to 6–2.
After their bye week, the Giants split their remaining eight games to finish with a record of 10–6.
The Giants were led by a productive rushing attack behind Brandon Jacobs, Derrick Ward, and Reuben Droughns.
Brandon Jacobs, Derrick Ward, and Reuben Droughns combined for almost 2,000 yards and 13 rushing touchdowns.
The Giants did not win their division, as the Dallas Cowboys went 13–3.
The Giants' record was good enough to secure the fifth seed and a Wild Card playoff berth.
The Giants beat the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the Wild Card round by a score of 24–8.
The Giants' victory over the Buccaneers earned them a match-up with the Cowboys.
The Giants beat the Cowboys 21–17 in the Divisional round to proceed to the NFC Championship Game.
The Packers missed the playoffs in 2006 with a record of 8–8, after losing out the playoff tiebreaker to the Giants.
The Packers finished the 2007 season with a record of 13–3, the same as the Cowboys.
The Packers' 2007 season included two losses to the Chicago Bears.
The Packers' other loss was to the Cowboys, which ended up being the tiebreaker for the first seed in the playoffs.
The Packers won the NFC North division.
With their head-to-head match-up loss, the Packers were given the second seed.
Brett Favre completed his 18th season with the Packers.
Brett Favre finished in the top 10 of most season passing statistics.
The Packers' defense gave up the sixth least amount of points during the season.
The Packers received a bye week in the Wild Card round before hosting the Seattle Seahawks in the Divisional round.
The Packers blew out the Seahawks 42–20 in what became known as the Snow Globe Game.
With their higher seeding, the Packers were scheduled to host the Giants at Lambeau Field on January 20, 2008, for the NFC Championship Game.
The Green Bay Press-Gazette predicted cold weather for the game, with the wind chill factor bringing the daily low down to −22 °F (−30 °C).
The National Weather Service issued a wind chill advisory prior to the start of the game.
The Packers were 7.5 point favorites.
The Packers started the game with possession.
The Packers were forced to punt after reaching mid-field on their first drive.
The Giants proceeded to drive 71 yards in 14 plays before the Packers stopped them on the 11-yard line.
Lawrence Tynes converted a field goal for the Giants, giving them a 3–0 lead.
The next three drives, two by the Packers and one by the Giants, ended in punts.
The Giants gained possession at mid-field after the last Packers punt.
The Giants again drove into field goal range.
The Packers again stopped the Giants on third down, forcing another field goal attempt.
Tynes made a 37-yard field goal to increase the Giants' lead to 6–0.
On the first play of the ensuing drive, Brett Favre completed a 90-yard touchdown pass to Donald Driver, giving the Packers a 7–6 lead.
The next three drives ended in punts, with the Packers regaining possession at mid-field.
After a short drive, Mason Crosby converted a 36-yard field goal, bringing the score to 10–6.
With just over a minute left in the half, the Giants drove 40 yards.
A sack on fourth down forced a turnover on downs for the Giants.
The Packers ran one play before halftime.
The Giants started the second half with the ball.
The Giants engineered a 12-play, 68-yard drive that culminated in a one-yard rushing touchdown by Brandon Jacobs.
Brandon Jacobs' touchdown gave the Giants the lead again, 13–10.
After a long return on the kick-off by Tramon Williams, the Packers started with a short field.
The Packers scored six plays later on a 12-yard touchdown pass from Favre to Donald Lee.
With the extra point, the Packers took the lead back, 17–13.
On the next drive, the Giants started near mid-field and drove for a touchdown.
Ahmad Bradshaw scored a rushing touchdown, bringing the score to 20–17.
The Packers tied the game on the next drive with a 37-yard field goal by Crosby.
The Packers had two more drives before the end of the game, both of which ended in three-and-outs.
The Giants' remaining three possessions ended in a punt and two missed field goals, including a 36-yard attempt as time expired in the fourth quarter.
The Packers won the coin toss before overtime and chose to receive the ball first.
On the second play of the drive, after a short rush, Favre threw a pass intended for Driver but was intercepted by Corey Webster.
On the ensuing drive, the Giants only gained five yards.
The Giants' drive set up a 47-yard field goal attempt.
Tynes converted the attempt to give the Giants the victory, 23–20.
The game was played at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin.
The game time was 6:30 p.m. EST/5:30 p.m. CST.
The weather at the game was −1 °F (−18 °C) and clear.
The attendance at the game was 72,740.
The game was broadcast on Fox.
The announcers for the game were Joe Buck, Troy Aikman, Pam Oliver, and Chris Myers.
In the 1st Quarter, Lawrence Tynes scored a 29-yard field goal for the New York Giants at 4:50, making the score Giants 3–0.
The drive for Tynes' 29-yard field goal consisted of 14 plays, covered 71 yards, and took 7 minutes and 48 seconds.
In the 2nd Quarter, Lawrence Tynes scored a 37-yard field goal for the New York Giants at 11:41, making the score Giants 6–0.
The drive for Tynes' 37-yard field goal consisted of 7 plays, covered 38 yards, and took 3 minutes and 4 seconds.
In the 2nd Quarter, Donald Driver scored a 90-yard pass from Brett Favre (Mason Crosby kick) for the Green Bay Packers at 11:18, making the score Packers 7–6.
The drive for Driver's 90-yard touchdown pass consisted of 1 play, covered 90 yards, and took 0 minutes and 23 seconds.
In the 2nd Quarter, Mason Crosby scored a 36-yard field goal for the Green Bay Packers at 1:30, making the score Packers 10–6.
The drive for Crosby's 36-yard field goal consisted of 8 plays, covered 29 yards, and took 2 minutes and 58 seconds.
In the 3rd Quarter, Brandon Jacobs scored a 1-yard run for the New York Giants at 7:56, making the score Giants 13–10.
The drive for Jacobs' 1-yard run consisted of 12 plays, covered 69 yards, and took 7 minutes and 4 seconds.
In the 3rd Quarter, Donald Lee scored a 12-yard pass from Brett Favre (Mason Crosby kick) for the Green Bay Packers at 5:00, making the score Packers 17–13.
The drive for Lee's 12-yard touchdown pass consisted of 6 plays, covered 39 yards, and took 2 minutes and 56 seconds.
In the 3rd Quarter, Ahmad Bradshaw scored a 4-yard run for the New York Giants at 2:12, making the score Giants 20–17.
The drive for Bradshaw's 4-yard run consisted of 7 plays, covered 57 yards, and took 2 minutes and 48 seconds.
In the 4th Quarter, Mason Crosby scored a 37-yard field goal for the Green Bay Packers at 11:46, tying the score 20–20.
The drive for Crosby's 37-yard field goal consisted of 4 plays, covered 0 yards, and took 2 minutes and 14 seconds.
In Overtime, Lawrence Tynes scored a 47-yard field goal for the New York Giants at 12:25, making the score Giants 23–20.
The drive for Tynes' 47-yard field goal consisted of 4 plays, covered 5 yards, and took 1 minute and 39 seconds.

Post-game analysis focused on the competitive nature of the game, the impacts of the weather, individual performances, and the question of Favre's future.
The Green Bay Press-Gazette commented that it appeared neither team truly wanted to win, with each giving the other multiple opportunities to secure a victory.

The Green Bay Press-Gazette noted that the game would be a game to remember for many years due to it going to overtime, being won on a walk-off field goal, the cold weather, and Favre's legacy in the balance.
The weather ended up making the game the second coldest in Lambeau Field history up to that point.
Temperatures dropped from −1 °F (−18 °C) at kick-off to −3 °F (−19 °C) by the end of the game.
The wind chill dropped as low as −24 °F (−31 °C) by the end of the game.
Giants' head coach Tom Coughlin's face became bright red during the game.
Sports commentators noted that the weather conditions also likely impacted the game, including on the late missed field goals by Lawrence Tynes.
Favre had just completed one of his most productive seasons of his career, finishing in second place in MVP voting.
The Packers had drafted Aaron Rodgers in 2005.
Favre had been contemplating retirement since at least 2006.
The way the game ended, with Favre throwing an interception, strengthened the belief that he would not commit to another season and retire.
Favre noted after the game that his decision would be made quickly, after talking with the Packers coaches.
Plaxico Burress led the offensive output for the Giants with 11 catches for 151 yards.
Plaxico Burress's 11 catches and 151 yards tied or set playoff records for players against the Packers.
Brandon Jacobs and Ahmad Bradshaw combined for a strong running game, gaining 130 yards on the ground and two touchdowns.
Ryan Grant only gained 29 yards on 13 rushes for the whole game.
The lack of a running game forced the Packers to be one-dimensional and rely on the passing game.
The Packers' offense fell apart in the second half, having one of their worst playoff halves in history.
Sports commentators noted that Favre appeared to be pressing his performance, trying to do too much and force throws to his receivers.
Individual plays and players were highlighted during the post-game analysis.
Favre's 90-yard touchdown pass to Donald Driver was the longest in Packers' playoff history at that time.
Favre's 90-yard touchdown pass to Donald Driver was identified as a key play of the game.
Favre's interception in overtime was a crucial mistake.
Favre noted that the interception came about because he did not throw the ball wide enough.
The Packers were unable to capitalize on Tynes' multiple missed field goals in the fourth quarter.
Tynes was highlighted for coming through in the end and not letting his earlier misses phase him.
Two fumbles were costly for different reasons.
Favre was intercepted in the fourth quarter, although R. W. McQuarters fumbled the ball on the return and the Packers recovered it.

On a punt return, the Giants fumbled the ball and Jarrett Bush tried to pick the ball up instead of falling on it and missed, allowing Domenik Hixon to recover it and retain possession for the Giants.
Other than the beginning of the second half, the Packers defense performed well.
Tramon Williams, A. J. Hawk, and Atari Bigby were all noted for their performance.
After their victory, the Giants moved on to Super Bowl XLII, where they faced the New England Patriots.
The Patriots, under Tom Brady, had completed a perfect 16–0 season.
The Patriots' 16–0 record was the first time an NFL team had a perfect regular season record under a 16-game season.
The Patriots also won two playoff games to advance to the Super Bowl.
The Patriots were attempting to become the first NFL team to win every regular and postseason game in a season since the 1972 Miami Dolphins.
The teams played a competitive game in Super Bowl XLII.
After the Patriots took the lead late in the game, the Giants drove down the field and scored.
The Giants' drive was aided by the famous Helmet Catch.
The Helmet Catch helped the Giants secure a 17–14 victory and the NFL Championship.
After the season, Favre announced his retirement.
Just a few months later, Favre rescinded his retirement and publicly stated his desire to return to the Packers for the 2008 NFL season.
The Packers publicly committed to Aaron Rodgers as Favre's successor.
After much discussion, Favre agreed to a trade to the New York Jets.
Rodgers was reaffirmed as the starter for the Packers in 2008.
Rodgers led the Packers to the playoffs in the 2009 season.
Rodgers won Super Bowl XLV in the 2010 season.
The game has been characterized by multiple sports commentators as one of the greatest championship games in league history.
In 2019, the league identified the game as the 54th greatest game from the first 100 years of the history of the NFL.
The game became an important part of the Giants–Packers rivalry, which had included five championship games before this one.
The game has been remembered for its cold weather, with Giants' coach Tom Coughlin's red face becoming an indelible image from the game.
The weather also impacted the play on the field and made Tynes' game-winning field goal even more improbable and memorable.
With Favre's retirement and then trade to the Jets after the season, the NFC Championship became the last game Favre would play in his career with the Packers.
Favre's last pass as a Packer was an interception.
The game was representative of Favre's playoff failures in the 2000s, where he lost six games and threw more interceptions than touchdowns.
For Eli Manning, the victory against the Packers and then the Patriots in the Super Bowl helped establish his quarterback credentials.
